summary.text: You may use eligible family members' MediSave and apply for Government assistance. If you still cannot pay, MediFund and ComCare may help.

details.heading: Why some MediSave is kept
details.body: The minimum MediSave Account balance under MediSave Care is set to help individuals maintain some savings for healthcare bills.

steps.name: Use your spouse's MediSave
steps.text: For long-term care withdrawals, you may tap on your spouse's MediSave.

steps.name: Use family MediSave
steps.text: For other healthcare treatments, you may tap on your family members' MediSave.

steps.name: Apply for assistance
steps.text: You may apply for means-tested Government assistance schemes, such as ElderFund and Home Caregiving Grant, for your long-term care costs.

steps.name: Seek further help
steps.text: If you still cannot pay after Government subsidies and other support, there are other forms of assistance such as MediFund and ComCare.

example_phrasings: What if I have insufficient MediSave balances for my healthcare and long-term care expenses?
What can I do if my MediSave runs out?
Can my family help with MediSave for my care?

sources.page_title: What if I have insufficient MediSave balances for my healthcare and long-term care expenses?

quotes.text: If you are still unable to pay for your care even after Government subsidies and other means of support, there are other forms of assistance such as MediFund and ComCare.
If you have depleted your MediSave account, you may tap on your spouse's MediSave for long-term care withdrawals, and your family members' MediSave for your other healthcare treatments.
You may also apply for other forms of assistance such as means-tested Government assistance schemes (ElderFund, Home Caregiving Grant) to meet your long-term care costs needs.
The minimum MediSave Account balance of $5,000 under MediSave Care is carefully set to help individuals maintain some savings to pay for for their healthcare bills.
